title: Latency + Cost UI: hypotheses & wireframes
content:
Purpose:
- Capture lightweight hypotheses and low-fi wireframe ideas for a single-screen Optimize Recommendations experience that makes batching, caching, and quantization suggestions easy to scan, simulate, and apply.
- This doc is intentionally iterative: sketches -> UX notes -> grooming backlog. Focus on developer mental model: impact-first, safe quick-apply, and explainable tradeoffs.

High-level constraints and goals:
- Primary persona: backend/ML engineer integrating Redwood into production (wants predictable latency and unit-cost improvement).
- Show estimated impact (latency percentile, cost per 1M tokens) for each recommendation before apply.
- Safe defaults: one-click canary (apply to 1% traffic) + preview simulation for 1, 10, 100 concurrent requests.
- Keep it compact: allow power users to deep-dive, keep quick actions front-and-center for PLG flow.

Proposed single-screen layout (wireframe notes):
- Left rail: "Suggested Actions" vertical list (compact rows). Each row shows: short label (e.g., "Auto-batch: 32->64"), top-line delta ("-18% cost, +12ms p95"), confidence pill (High/Medium/Low), and a quick-apply toggle. Row is keyboard-focusable.
- Center detail pane: when a suggestion is selected, show an explainer card with: motivation, technical change (literal config diff snippet), estimated unit economics, risk notes, compatibility (models/hw), and acceptance criteria for rollout. Include an inline micro-chart showing cost vs latency tradeoff curve for that recommendation.
- Right preview panel: small scenario simulator — choose sample workload (dropdown: small chat, Q&A, embeddings batch) and run quick simulation for configured concurrency. Show simulated p50/p95, tokens/sec, and estimated monthly cost change. Include a simple "what-if" slider for traffic % routed to this config.
- Top bar: filter chips (by model family, environment: staging/prod, hardware), a search box for free-text, and an "Apply Preset" dropdown (conservative/balanced/aggressive).
- Contextual help: inline tooltip icons that link to short blurbs or to a full doc. Use the same microcopy as Redwood Console.

Wireframe variants (quick sketches to test):
1) Compact list-first: left rail rows show full summary + micro-sparkline; selecting expands detail below the fold. Advantage: quick scan. Risk: hides simulator.
2) Detail-first split: Center shows currently selected suggestion large; left becomes thin index. Advantage: forces review before apply. Risk: slower for power users.
3) Preset-driven canvas: show small set of curated prescriptive bundles (e.g., "Latency SLO: 100ms", "Cost target: -20%"), with recommendations grouped beneath. Advantage: higher-level entry.

Interaction patterns (notes):
- Quick apply button opens a small modal for canary config: percent, duration, auto-rollback threshold. Pre-populate with safe defaults (1% for 1 hour, rollback if p95 > baseline by 20%).
- Inline "simulate" should not require provisioning; it uses lightweight historical traces + cost model. Show confidence band (low/med/high) linked to data freshness.
- Changes are auditable: every apply generates an entry in rollout history with diff + who applied + link to related ticket.

Backlog grooming (initial tickets & rough sizing):
- OPX-1001: UI scaffold for suggestions screen (5 days) — header, rail, empty state. Acceptance: static prototype with sample suggestion rows.
- OPX-1002: Suggestion row component + keyboard nav (3 days) — row visuals, quick-apply toggle. Acceptance: keyboard nav works, toggles reflect state.
- OPX-1003: Detail pane + config diff renderer (4 days) — show JSON/YAML snippet, risk notes. Acceptance: accurate diff rendering for mock suggestions.
- OPX-1004: Mini-simulator backend hook (8 days) — endpoint to run quick sim using stored traces and cost model. Acceptance: returns p50/p95 + cost delta for scenarios.
- OPX-1005: Canary modal + rollout API integration (5 days) — send canary request to rollout service. Acceptance: canary created and shows in Rollouts page.
- OPX-1006: Preset manager + UX (6 days) — preset creation, apply, and list. Acceptance: save / apply preset in prototype.
- OPX-1007: A11y pass + microcopy polish (2 days) — keyboard labels, aria, tooltip copy. Acceptance: passes basic accessibility checklist.

Acceptance criteria templates (copy for each ticket):
- Given a user with project access, when they open the Optimize Suggestions page, then they can scan rows and see estimated impact numbers.
- Given a selected suggestion, when they click "simulate", then a preview appears within 5s with p50/p95 and cost delta.
- Given a user clicks quick-apply and confirms, then a canary rollout is created and visible in Rollouts.

Open questions / risks to resolve in next 2 sprints:
- Data freshness: how often are workload traces available to the simulator? (ask infra/assertions queue).
- Cost model accuracy across quantization variants (need research & applied-ml signoff).
- Ownership: who curates low/medium/high confidence? (options: research, applied-ml, or heuristics team).
- Rollout safety: auto-rollback thresholds should be configurable per-org; add to RBAC discussion.

User testing plan (next steps):
- Rapid hallway tests (5 engineers) using InVision prototype — focus on scanability and trust cues.
- 2 customer interviews with platform engineers at pilot accounts (request via solutions-eng).
- Measure success: % of suggestions applied as canary, reduction in median cost per token, and time-to-apply metric.

Notes to UX writers / design ops:
- Tone: pragmatic, developer-first. Use short imperative labels: "Apply canary", "Simulate impact", "View diff".
- Microcopy for confidence: prefer "High (data-backed)" over star ratings.
- Illustrations: avoid heavy metaphors — prefer small charts and code diff snippets.

Slack references / context links:

- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/842
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Optimize+Hypotheses

Next meeting agenda (sync with product/research/design):
- Walkthrough prototype (15m)
- Review simulator assumptions and sample traces (10m)
- Prioritize backlog tickets and assign owners (10m)
- Agree on pilot customers and success metrics (5m)

Owners and immediate action items:
- Maya Chen: build static prototype (OPX-1001) and coordinate prototype tests.
- Arjun Patel: validate cost model with applied-ml and produce quick reference doc.
- Sofia Morales: draft microcopy and prepare user test script.

Appendix: sample suggestion examples (for filler data) — each line is a mock suggestion we can seed the prototype with:
- "Auto-batch: 32 -> 64" | Impact: -18% cost / +12ms p95 | Confidence: Medium | Compatibility: decoder-only LLMs
- "Prefix KV-caching: enable" | Impact: -25% cost (for repeated prompts) | Confidence: High | Notes: best for chat sessions from authenticated users
- "Quantize: int8 on GPU A100" | Impact: -35% cost / +6ms p95 | Confidence: Low | Notes: test for model quality regression on eval set
- "Dynamic batch: enable up to 128" | Impact: -22% cost / varies on traffic pattern | Confidence: Medium
